correction: Appended an explanatory diagram of Phi: E(A) -> Pi(A), R |-> A/R and Psi: Pi(A) -> E(A), P |-> sim_P, with both inverse identities. Existing Statement, Facts, Proof, title and all frontmatter remain byte-identical.

diagram_math_checks.result: E(A) denotes equivalence relations on the fixed set A (relations are subsets of A x A by def-equivalence-relation); Pi(A) denotes partitions satisfying the exact three conditions in the Statement. Phi sends R to A/R. Claims 1 and 3, proved in steps 1.1 and 2.2, ensure this is a partition of the same A. Psi sends P to the relation sim_P; step 2.3 verifies reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity, so Psi has the depicted codomain.

The upper arrow points E(A) to Pi(A) and is labelled Phi; the lower arrow points Pi(A) to E(A) and is labelled Psi. The accompanying prose defines the construction of each. For each a in A, step 1.3 gives its unique block B_a, and step 3.1 proves [a]_P=B_a. No representative-selection function or Choice assumption is introduced.

For P in Pi(A), step 4.1 gives Phi(Psi(P))=A/sim_P=P. For R in E(A), take P=A/R. Both R and sim_P are equivalence relations with quotient P, so uniqueness in step 4.2 gives Psi(Phi(R))=R. The figure asserts these identities only; it does not assert additional functorial, categorical or topological structure.

If A is empty, any partition has no nonempty block, hence must be empty; the sole relation on A is empty and is vacuously an equivalence relation. Both constructions and identities still apply. The existing 10-step rigorous proof is unchanged and precedes the figure; the added prose explicitly states its independence.
